title: Sci-MMR: Benchmarking Multi-Step Evidence-Grounded Scientific Reasoning in Multimodal Agents

rejected_items.claim: The benchmark construction uses a human-in-the-loop pipeline with deterministic validation removing 54% of candidate tasks, an eight-dimensional rubric filtering a further 17%, and final expert review of 260 tasks yielding 235 retained tasks.
rejected_items.explanation: The construction flow is documented with specific stage rates and expert-review dispositions, including independent dual review and adjudication, supporting the rigor of the pipeline.

Task generation.From each verified Argument
Graph, we sample a argument subgraph suffi-
cient to derive a target claim. The sampled graph
specifies the required observations, intermediate
claims, and scientific knowledge, from which an
LLM generates a natural multi-hop question with-

answers are generated independently from the
complete argument graph, presenting grounded
observations, intermediate reasoning, and the fi-
nal conclusion in dependency order with explicit
figure and table attributions.

numeric_rejections.claim: Error decomposition of 1,014 incorrect Direct Visual Reasoning outputs attributes 57.2% of errors to evidence-related failures and 31.8% to reasoning-related failures, supporting the two-bottleneck conclusion.
numeric_rejections.explanation: The routing procedure and subtype counts are reported in the main text and appendix, with sensitivity analysis at IoU thresholds 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7 showing the access/localization subtype remains largest, aligning evidence with the claimed bottlenecks.
